table_px_to_mm — MEASURE1D scale op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.table_px_to_mm(table, mm_per_px, keys=('width', 'radius', 'dist', 'rms', 'ra', 'rb', 'l1', 'l2')) (to call the implementation directly, import measuring1d; measuring1d.table_px_to_mm(table, mm_per_px, keys=('width', 'radius', 'dist', 'rms', 'ra', 'rb', 'l1', 'l2')); from the registry, opsmeasure1d.get("table_px_to_mm"))

Usage

Adds mm columns to a measurement table (the return of measure_pairs / apply_metrology_model).

For every numeric column k listed in keys it adds k_mm = k * mm_per_px (the px columns stay — removing them would cut the provenance). Each row of apply_metrology_model holds radius / l1 … inside a params dict, so that is converted too. The input is a list[dict] or a single dict; a shallow copy is returned and the input is not modified.

• Non-numeric or missing columns are skipped silently (whether a column was converted shows as the presence of k_mm).

• mm_per_px must be finite and positive (the value from mm_per_px_from_reference).

• rms is the fit residual [px]; in mm it compares directly with a tolerance.

• An empty table ([] / {}) raises ValueError (so that "no row at all" is not hidden behind the conversion).
